front: Name the 5 marks of a male California quail.
back: Curled black plume, black face rimmed in white, scaled belly, chestnut belly patch, white streaks on grey brown sides (80%).

front: How do you tell a female California quail?
back: Plain grey brown face, small brown plume, no black face or white rim. Same scaled belly (80%).

front: Weight and length of a California quail?
back: 140 to 230 g, 24 to 27 cm long (75%, Audubon).

front: Quail, Hun, chukar weights: the number trick?
Straight upright plume, barred red sides. Shoot?
back: No. Mountain quail: no open season (99%). Shoot California quail only.

front: How do you age a young quail in fall?
back: Buff tips on the upper primary coverts and pointed outer flight feathers (70%).

front: Chukar field marks?
back: Red bill and legs, black band through the eye to a necklace, barred black, white and chestnut flanks. 538 to 765 g (75%).

front: Gray partridge (Hun) field marks?
back: Orange face, chestnut horseshoe on the belly, rusty outer tail in flight. 300 to 500 g (75%).

front: When were California quail introduced to BC?
back: Between 1860 and 1912 (85%, BC Breeding Bird Atlas).

front: Two main BC quail areas?
back: Okanagan and Kettle valleys, and southeast Vancouver Island (85%). Fraser Valley birds appear gone (85%).

front: BC quail harvest, then and now?
back: Up to 4,600 a year in the 1970s, under 1,000 a year recently (65%, BC Outdoors).

front: Where in BC did chukar take hold best?
back: Low slopes of the Thompson from Kamloops to Lytton; also South Okanagan and Similkameen (65%).

front: Where are a quail's heart and lungs?
back: Front half: lungs high under the back between the ribs, heart low behind the crop (70%).

front: How many air sacs does a fowl have?
back: Nine. They pump air but do not exchange gas (70%, poultry anatomy).

front: What pumps air in a bird, with no diaphragm?
back: The ribs and breastbone, moving the air sacs (70%).

front: How many breaths for one gulp of air to pass through?
back: Two: rear sacs, lung, front sacs, out. Fresh air crosses the lung both ways (70%).

front: What does the crop do? The gizzard?
back: Crop stores a meal. Gizzard grinds it with grit (70%).

front: Field trick with the crop?
back: Open it after the hunt: it shows what the covey eats right now (Tip).

front: Why are quail flights short?
back: Breast muscle is mostly white fibre: fast, little staying power. Burst, glide, land, run (70%).

front: Fowl body temperature?
back: About 41 to 41.7 °C (70%, chicken figure).

front: Hot weather water rule for quail?
back: Free water every day in hot weather; dew and green plants are enough in cool weather (80%).

front: How long do quail live?
back: Few past one year; about six years at most (65%). Most of a fall covey is young.

front: Early banding study: of 101 quail, how many seen at 1 year?
back: 15. Then 4 at two years, 1 at three (60%).

front: Which sense does a quail trust most?
back: Eyes, then ears. Nose is weak (70 to 85%).

front: How wide is the chicken's two eyed (binocular) field?
back: About 26°. The rest is seen one eye at a time; near full circle view (70%).

front: How many colour cone types do birds have?
back: Four, including ultraviolet. Humans have three (85%).

front: Best hearing band of birds?
back: About 1 to 4 kHz: voices, boots on gravel, gun clicks (75%).

front: Who watches while the covey feeds?
back: A sentinel, usually a male, on a high perch. He gives the alarm (70%).

front: How far from cover do quail feed?
back: Seldom more than 15 to 30 m (80%).

front: Does scent control matter for quail?
back: Little. Smell is weak in fowl (70%). Wind still carries your noise and helps a dog (Tip).

front: What is the assembly call and when is it given?
back: "Chi CA go", loudest middle note. A separated bird, or a covey on the move; repeated 10 or more times (70%).

front: Spring call of an unpaired cock?
back: One loud "cow" from a high perch (70%).

front: What is the "squill" call?
back: Males fighting over rank in spring (70%).

front: A quail's first answer to danger?
back: Run into cover. Fly as a last resort (70%).

front: After a covey flush, what do singles do?
back: Land a few dozen yards off, hold tight, then call to regroup (75%).

front: When does the dusk chorus happen and why?
back: At dusk, scattered birds call as they gather to roost (75%).

front: Huns flushed twice: what next?
back: They flush farther each time. Make the first chance count (75%).

front: Typical BC covey size?
back: Usually under 30, sometimes 100 or more (85%).

front: Who gets mates in a covey?
back: Males in the dominance hierarchy; older birds pair earlier (70%).

front: California winter range of a covey?
back: About 10.5 ha, from 6.9 to 18 ha (80%).

front: When do coveys break up?
back: March; about 2 months to sort into pairs (70%).

front: Clutch and incubation?
back: About 14 eggs; the hen sits 22 to 23 days (80%).

front: When do chicks fly?
back: Short hops at about 10 days; they run within a day of hatching (75%).

front: Peak hatch month?
back: June (80%, California records). BC may run later: VERIFY.

front: What drives a good hatch?
back: Rain and green growth the winter and spring before (80%).

front: Region 8 quail season and limits?
back: 1 October to 30 November, 10 a day, 30 in possession, MUs 8-1 to 8-15 and 8-21 to 8-26 (99%).

front: Best window inside the season (Tip)?
back: Late October to mid November: leaves down, coveys formed (Tip).

front: Chukar clutch and incubation?
back: 10 to 20 eggs, average 15; about 24 days (80%, FEIS).

front: What do chukar do in deep snow?
back: Move to lower ground and south slopes (80%).

front: When do quail feed in fall?
back: Twice: just after dawn and late afternoon (70%).

front: What do quail do at midday?
back: Loaf in cover, dust bathe, drink (75%).

front: When do quail pick grit?
back: Before the morning and afternoon feeds, at road edges (75%).

front: Storm day behaviour?
back: They feed in the breaks of the storm (70%).

front: Cold fronts and moon: proven effects?
back: No good quail data. Tip only.

front: Covey flew up into trees. What now?
back: Walk away, come back in 30 to 60 minutes (75%). No shots at sitting birds (Tip).

front: Where are chukar late in the afternoon?
back: Moving back up to steeper roost areas (75%).

front: Legal hunting hours for quail?
back: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset (99%).

front: BC quail elevation band?
back: Mostly 250 to 500 m, rarely above 750 m (85%).

front: Which biogeoclimatic zones hold Interior quail?
back: Ponderosa Pine and Bunchgrass (85%).

front: Key plant of chukar country?
back: Cheatgrass (80%), with sage, bitterbrush and rock.

front: Quail at Heffley Creek legal?
back: No. Region 3 has no quail row (97%). Chukar and Huns are open there (99%).

front: Quail near Mission?
back: No quail row in Region 2 (97%) and the Fraser Valley birds appear gone (85%).

front: First three Hunt Map layers for quail?
back: California quail habitat, Private land, City and town limits (Tip).

front: Which terrain tool shows warm, snow free slopes?
back: Slope direction: south slopes warm and melt first (75% for chukar use).

front: Which Hunt Map area to download for the quail trip?
back: Area C: South Okanagan and Similkameen (95%).

front: How do quail tracks lie?
back: Three toes forward, short hind toe, prints in one line (60%).

front: Quail track length?
back: About 3.5 cm: Tip, VERIFY. Grouse about 5 cm (75%).

front: What is the white cap on a dropping?
back: Uric acid, the bird's nitrogen waste (70%).

front: Where do California quail roost?
back: Dense trees or shrubs, not on the ground (70%). Look for piles under them.

front: Three signs that say quail are near a lane?
back: Tracks, droppings and dusting holes (75%).

front: Is a mouth quail call legal? An electronic one?
back: Mouth call: yes (95%, my reading). Recorded or electronic calls for game birds: no (99%).

front: Steps to follow a covey?
back: Listen at dawn or dusk, read sign on the lanes, stop and go along cover, mark the singles (Tip, 75%).

front: Is an unsigned orchard open to hunt?
back: No. Cultivated land needs consent of the owner, lessee or occupant (99%). Orchards count (95%).

front: The 100 m rule?
back: No hunting or shooting within 100 m of a dwelling, school, playground or occupied farm building (99%).

front: Are town bylaws in the synopsis?
back: No (99%). Hunt outside every town boundary.

front: Vernon Bylaw 5399 says?
back: No discharge of a firearm, air guns included, inside the city (99%).

front: How long to stop on a stop and go?
back: 15 to 20 seconds at each patch of cover (75%).

front: How far apart do two hunters walk a draw?
back: 15 to 25 m, level, each owning one side (Tip).

front: Where do most hunters miss a straightaway quail?
back: High. Hold a hair under (75%).

front: Best time to hunt singles?
back: Right after the flush, while they hold tight (75%).

front: Tall Timbers manners rule for a covey?
back: Three or more birds from a rise, then let the covey go (Tip, 60%).

front: How to approach chukar?
back: From above; then follow the same contour line (75%).

front: Huns: the key tactic?
back: Cover a lot of ground; feed edges of grain fields, hide in hay, grass, fence lines (75%).

front: Are dogs legal for quail?
back: Yes, unleashed dogs may hunt small game (99%).

front: Standard quail loads and choke?
back: Lead 7.5 or 8 (steel 6 or 7), skeet or improved cylinder (75%).

front: Is lead shot legal for quail?
back: Yes, the shot ban does not apply to upland game birds (99%).

front: Plug rule?
back: No more than 3 shells in total in a pump or auto (95%).

front: A bird falls as another flushes. First move?
back: Mark the fall, drop your hat, walk straight to it (60%). Retrieval is the law (99%).

front: What must stay on a quail until home?
back: One feathered wing (99%). Both breasts go home (99%).

front: Meat from one quail?
back: About 60 to 80 g (Tip, 60%).

front: Safe cooking temperature for birds?
Region 8 chukar and Hun limits?
back: Chukar 5 (15), gray partridge 3 (9), 1 Oct to 30 Nov (99%).

front: Legal firearms for quail?
back: Shotgun, air gun or bows B, C, D. No .22, no centrefire (95%).

front: Licence needed for quail as a BC resident?
back: The BC hunting licence only, no species licence (99%).
